# Synthetic account compatibility corpus

`oracle.json` contains267synthetic input cases and the unchanged frozen JavaScript validator's accepted canonical result or rejection. It includes supported input versions1–11 (minimal and rich-history cases), every supported root entity, historical line prices/names, reversals, partial returns, legacy catalog migration, compatibility-only worker/savings records, preferences and explicit invalid/reference/numeric/date cases. The180seeded cases use seed`0x02002610`; these are deterministic generated cases without automatic shrinking.

Source: `electron-reference/app/ui/model.js`, SHA256`65a9b33cdca42e328d710f1afaa1b0fb42a7778284bd2f07f7c7e77d3d9f07f4`. Node version and timezone from generation are retained in the manifest. `node scripts/build-account-corpus.cjs --check` reruns the actual frozen validator and compares cases and source hash; host Node/timezone metadata is reported rather than required to match the original generation host. All data is authored test data; this is not a released-installation migration rehearsal or a production-account snapshot.

`test/accounts/codec_test.dart` compares all accepted fields recursively, checks all rejected inputs, canonical roundtrip and normalization idempotence, independent immutable historical relationships, unsupported/invalid error distinction, UTF8/numeric handling and independent incoming/normalized-output20MiB limits. Portable output uses two-space indented JSON, preserving the source save-size acceptance profile. The output-limit regression builds200000unique valid expenses whose compact input fits20MiB but normalized output exceeds it.

Timestamp compatibility retains original text and tests source ISO, date-only/year-only, US and RFC forms, invalid hour/month/minute, overflow calendar day, hour24 and zero-year behavior. Independent-review regressions additionally cover legacy numeric/English TimeClip limits, source EST/date-only-Z spellings and MAXSAFE remainder neighbors whose temporary prefix exceeds the final-value bound. The remainder compatibility profile preserves the frozen operator grouping and binary64 integer-rounding acceptance through an explicit BigInt-only engine helper; exact and strict-prefix policies remain separate. The finite oracle corpus is evidence for the listed cases, not a proof over every implementation-dependent JavaScript `Date.parse` spelling. The consumer's parser must remain subject to independent compatibility review before release. Generic arithmetic/date/identifier rules are consumed from `madar_domain`; restaurant field names, references, migration meanings and source-specific string/timestamp compatibility remain here.

Recreate only after inspecting an intentional frozen-source/provenance change. Neither the generator nor tests open installed restaurant files or modify the frozen source.
